summary: Every input row requires its own classification and output row, so the single constant-time CASE evaluation per row matches the linear output lower bound.

optimality.argument: The result contains one classification for each of n input rows, requiring Omega(n) output work; the query performs a constant number of additions and comparisons per row.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each of the n distinct input rows contributes one mandatory result classification.
One CASE expression applies a constant number of triangle and equality comparisons to each row.
Cases cover all classes, degeneracy, every possible largest-side position, equality pairs, permutations, and row multiplicity.
